question: A user is having a quick, one-off conversation with Claude to brainstorm five possible names for a new podcast. The conversation does not need to be revisited later or reference any uploaded files. Which feature is the most appropriate fit for this task?
options: A) A new Project created specifically to store the podcast name brainstorm
B) An artifact, so the list of names appears in a dedicated side panel
C) Research mode, so Claude searches the web for existing podcast names to avoid
D) A standard chat conversation, without creating a Project or enabling research mode
correct_answers: D) A standard chat conversation, without creating a Project or enabling research mode
explanations: Creating a Project adds persistent knowledge-base structure that is unnecessary overhead for a single one-off brainstorm that won't be revisited.
A short list of five names is not substantial, standalone content requiring iterative editing, so an artifact is not needed for this simple exchange.
Enabling research mode to search the web for existing podcast names is unnecessary for a quick five-name brainstorm and would add latency without meaningful benefit.

Correct. A short, self-contained brainstorming task with no need for persistent knowledge or external research fits naturally into a standard chat conversation without the added structure of a Project, research mode, or an artifact.
